relevance_result.response_opportunity: Explain how Raft's randomized election timeouts prevent the split-vote deadlock scenario you described, specifically how the randomness ensures that not all nodes will timeout simultaneously and how this resolves potential leader election deadlocks.

suggestions.text: Raft uses randomized election timeouts precisely to avoid this. Even if three nodes timeout at the same moment and split their votes, no candidate reaches a majority, so the election fails for that term. Everyone steps back to follower, increments the term, and picks a new random timeout. Because the timeouts are randomized, the nodes won't wake up together again, so one candidate will eventually gather a majority and win. There's no perpetual deadlock loop.
suggestions.rationale: Directly addresses the split-vote deadlock concern by explaining how randomized timeouts break synchronization and allow eventual convergence, without diving into term number proofs.

suggestions.text: Think of it like this: a split vote isn't a permanent tie, it's just a failed election for that term. The randomness ensures the next round starts at different times, so the cluster quickly moves past the tie.
suggestions.rationale: Offers an intuitive analogy that reinforces why the deadlock resolves itself, keeping the explanation concise and accessible.
